subject: Re: LumaTech migration — pilot credit & commercial offer
messages:
From: Elaine Jenkins <elaine.jenkins@luma.tech>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluating migration — ask on credits and onboarding

Hi Michael,

We had a sync internally this morning about replacing our incumbent inference vendor. Two priorities: 1) keep near-term inference spend flat (cost-neutral migration for Q4) and 2) accelerate quality/latency improvements for our real-time use cases.

Before we move deeper: could Redwood share a migration incentive structure (pilot credits, onboarding support, any one-time credits) and a short-term TCO comparison for our profile? I attached a small usage export (last 3 months) to help.

High level: ~180M tokens/month, ~50% real-time low-latency traffic, some batch embedding jobs nightly. Our current deal has a 9-month notice and we want a plan that would let us run a 60–90 day pilot without materially increasing cash outlay in Q4.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Jenkins
Head of Platform Engineering, LumaTech
elaine.jenkins@luma.tech
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: current_usage_export.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Jenkins <elaine.jenkins@luma.tech>
Date: 2026-08-31T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating migration — ask on credits and onboarding

Hi Elaine — thanks for the context and the export.

Quick answers up front: we can do a timeboxed pilot with credits that approximate the delta to your incumbent for the pilot period, plus a dedicated onboarding window with our Migration Success team. For a usage profile like yours I want to confirm a couple of things before I send a commercial sketch:
- Which region will be primary (us-west/us-east/eu)?
- Do you require private deployment (VPC) or is hosted API acceptable for the pilot?
- Any non-negotiable security evidence (SOC2 + additional checks)?

If you can confirm by EOD tomorrow I’ll share a short commercial-term-sheet and a pilot SOW draft that Marissa (my manager) will review.

Short note on approach: typical structure we propose for migration pilots to be cost-neutral:
- Pilot credit that offsets per-token delta for 60–90 days
- One-time onboarding credit (hours with our Migration Success engineers)
- Roll-forward credit applied to committed spend in first 3 months post-pilot

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
+1 650-555-0199
From: Elaine Jenkins <elaine.jenkins@luma.tech>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating migration — ask on credits and onboarding

Michael — thanks.

Answers: primary region = us-east, hosted API is fine for pilot (we want to avoid heavy infra lift initially). SOC2 is required; we already have copies but procurement will want to see the latest reports.

A couple more details on traffic mix:
- 50% low-latency (<150ms target), peak concurrency ~600 requests/s during business hours.
- 40% batch embeddings overnight (~8 hours window).
- 10% experimental high-throughput training-adjacent workloads (tolerant of increased latency).

Procurement asked for an illustrative commercial sketch including: pilot credit amount, any seat-based or tiered discounts, and estimated monthly run-rate post-pilot for three pricing scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive). We need something tangible for our internal finance + legal review.

If you can get something by Thu I’ll route to procurement.

—Elaine

Subject: Re: Evaluating migration — illustrative pilot & commercial sketch

Elaine — attaching a short SOW and commercial-term-sheet per your ask. High-level proposal below.

Proposal (illustrative) — LumaTech profile (us-east)
1) Pilot window: 90 days, credit pool = $30,000 applied to API usage (covers the per-token delta and a portion of engineering hours).
2) Onboarding: 40 hours of Migration Success support (remote), included in the pilot credit; additional hours billed at our standard SOW rates.
3) Post-pilot commercial options (monthly run-rate after pilot):
   - Conservative: S1 (no commit) — pay-as-you-go; est. $48k/month
   - Expected: S2 (6-month commit) — 12% reduction; est. $42k/month
   - Aggressive: S3 (12-month commit + reserved capacity) — 25% reduction; est. $36k/month + 30% dedicated capacity guarantee
4) Timeboxed match: if you sign an S2 or S3 within 30 days of pilot completion we will apply an additional onboarding credit equal to 25% of the pilot credit to your first invoice.

Attachments: pilot-sow.pdf (SOW draft), commercial-term-sheet.pdf (pricing scenarios + assumptions). I pulled the numbers conservatively using your export; if real-time peak concurrency is higher we can tweak reserved capacity numbers.

If that looks directionally right I’ll ask Marissa to prepare a formal term-sheet and Naomi to confirm billing/contracting cadence. Also happy to set a 30-minute walkthrough to walk procurement/legal through the SOW.

Thanks — Michael

Attachment: pilot-sow.pdf (PDF, 18KB); commercial-term-sheet.pdf (XLSX, 24KB)
From: Elaine Jenkins <elaine.jenkins@luma.tech>

Date: 2026-09-07T14:37:00-07:00

Michael — this is helpful, thank you. I’ve shared the SOW and term sheet with our procurement team. A couple of notes from procurement/legal:
- We’ll need a 60-day review window internally; procurement may request small legal redlines (standard).
- Please include a clear statement on data retention and isolation for the pilot period in the SOW.
- Can you confirm whether the pilot credit is refundable or purely a usage credit (we prefer usage credit applied to invoices).

Next steps: I’ll loop procurement into the thread after their initial review. If you can confirm the data-retention language and that the credit is usage-only, procurement will move this to their 60-day review queue.

Also please CC whoever will own contracting so they have visibility.

Best,
Elaine
